summary: event-emitter-testmetest ships an obfuscated AES-GCM dropper executed at install and import time
details: The package's `main` (index.js) is a multi-layer obfuscated loader: a String.fromCharCode-reconstructed string is Caesar-shifted (k=19) and eval'd, which then AES-128-GCM-decrypts a hardcoded hex ciphertext using embedded key/iv/authTag and executes the plaintext via a dynamic `Function(module, require, process, Buffer, __filename, __dirname, <plaintext>)` call, giving the decrypted bytes full Node module, require, and process access. The payload is opaque to any installer. `binding.gyp` declares a target with no native source files and uses GYP command-expansion (`<!(env node index.js...)`) in `sources`, which runs the loader during `node-gyp rebuild` — npm invokes node-gyp automatically whenever `binding.gyp` is present, so the loader runs on `npm install` even though `package.json.scripts` contains no install hook. The same loader also executes whenever another module `require`s this package. The stacked charcode+Caesar+AES-GCM obfuscation and the use of a no-sources `binding.gyp` purely to trigger node-gyp are consistent only with hiding and auto-executing attacker-controlled code against the installer host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
